review_kind: independent full declared PRIMARY-SOURCE review of frozen paired outputs

reviewer_context.account_inspection: None; no credentials or account changes.

rules_application: Skipped pm-mail/extra-worker rules inside T3. No children, repository/canon changes, account actions, installers or external writes. Review files and all executed fixtures stay in the mapped output directory. No repository governance/build work was relevant.
evidence_semantics: SHA-256 confirms byte identity only. Behavioral conclusions come from inspected primary bodies and callers. Reviewer execution uses exact mapped library code on an existing host, not complete exact-release runtimes.
evidence_locators: Every primary source_id in claim/defect line locators resolves to the exact path, URL, release and SHA-256 in input_evidence.primary_sources. Candidate final.md locators resolve to each frozen artifact in input_evidence.frozen_outputs.
materiality_basis: Material defects affect a declared source-dependent security/API/compatibility disposition or a proposed regression's expected result. Locator precision and additional optional hint/test coverage are separately classified; no economic ranking, target grade or winner was used.

With both per-call filter and extraction_filter unset, 3.12.3 emits DeprecationWarning and selects fully_trusted_filter; 3.14.0 selects data_filter without that warning. The stored attribute remains None.
The named-filter ladder, wrapper names, ordinary metadata masking/nulling and direct special-file/link refusal branches are retained, with realpath and linkname changes requiring separate conditions.

Per-call callable/named filter configuration, rejection of string extraction_filter values, unknown-name ValueError and documented instance/subclass/global staticmethod mechanics remain. The old early-opt-in rationale changes.
The two handler bodies and standard errorlevel=1/2 fatal/nonfatal split persist; extraction may be partial and callers own cleanup. This narrower fact does not support retaining all refusal behavior.

Data alone remains insufficient for untrusted input: prior inspection, caller limits and cleanup considerations persist, including DoS, repeated-member overwrite and live-directory tampering limitations.
Capability detection/backport guidance and inspection APIs remain. numeric_owner is present but data nulls ownership metadata; explicit data is recommended for older runtimes supporting the feature.
The remaining tarnew DeprecationWarnings inspected concern TarInfo.tarfile removal in 3.16, not the omitted extraction default.
Output1 correctly carries the normalization symlink-meaning caveat and new optional symlink-disallow hint.

defects.claim: The prior F4 refusal/skip behavior and errorlevel contract can be retained unchanged at both exact releases.
defects.assessment: False for a filter refusal suppressed by errorlevel=0. In 3.12.3 the failed assignment leaves tarinfo equal to the original member, and extraction continues with that member. In 3.14.0 filtered starts as None and a suppressed refusal excludes the member. Identical handlers and identical documentation do not make these caller paths identical.

primary_evidence.symbol: old prose says skip despite implementation

counterexample.observed: With explicit data and errorlevel=0, the 3.12.3 library creates the FIFO; the 3.14.0 library skips it. At errorlevel=1 and 2 both raise SpecialFileError.
counterexample.limitation: Exact source modules on existing host CPython 3.14.4, not full exact-release interpreter runs; the decisive branch difference is also visible directly in the frozen implementation.

defects.consequences: Incorrect security and compatibility disposition of F4 and U2; documentation must not override the selected released implementation.

output_specific.Output1: Explicitly reports identical contracts and retains F4.
output_specific.Output2: Says prior F4 stands after comparing handler identifiers. Its qualified uncertainty does not repair this affirmative retention.

defects.kind: public API/security change misclassified or omitted
defects.claim: The refusal taxonomy is unchanged / the error taxonomy can be wholly classified as retained.
defects.assessment: The original five subclasses remain, but 3.14.0 adds the public LinkFallbackError and changes extractall fallback to re-filter the referenced archive member. This is a consequential change, not a renamed old class. extract() and extractall() also differ in propagation of the fallback filter in this exact file.

primary_evidence.symbol: extract does not pass filter_function to _extract_one

counterexample.observed: Select a hardlink whose earlier archived target is a FIFO absent on disk. With explicit data, 3.12.3 extractall creates a FIFO at the link path; 3.14.0 extractall raises LinkFallbackError caused by SpecialFileError. In the exact 3.14.0 library extract() still creates the FIFO in this fixture.
counterexample.limitation: Selected-member archive fixture; existing host interpreter. Since 3.14.0 resolves an omitted filter to this same data_filter, applicability to that default is a source-based inference, not a separately executed omitted-filter extraction.

defects.consequences: Exception handling, security and regression coverage need the new class and fallback conditions; an unqualified fail-closed description across extraction APIs is too broad.

output_specific.Output1: The explicit unchanged-taxonomy statement is false. It notices directory plumbing but misses this public addition.
output_specific.Output2: The narrow statement that the old five are preserved is true. The defect is its whole-taxonomy retained disposition and omission of the new public exception and fallback behavior, rather than denial that the old five still exist.

defects.claim: An ordinary absolute-path regular member on Linux raises AbsolutePathError under data; Output1 also expects a setuid regular member to raise a FilterError.
defects.assessment: Leading Linux slashes are stripped. A remaining absolute path is the conditional refusal, exemplified by Windows drive paths. A regular file's high mode bits are cleared rather than refused. Linux /safe_absolute_regular becomes safe_absolute_regular; regular mode 0o4755 becomes 0o755.

primary_evidence.symbol: strip leading slashes, conditional absolute refusal, mode rewrite
same conditional path and mode branches

counterexample.observed: Both exact library files accept and transform these regular members; no FilterError is raised.
counterexample.limitation: Direct filter checks on existing host, no outside-scope extraction.

defects.consequences: Proposed tests would incorrectly reject intended behavior. Ordinary sanitized members must be distinguished from absolute links, outside destinations and special files.

output_specific.Output1: Both the absolute regular file and setuid regular file assertions are wrong. Its absolute symlink and FIFO rejection expectations are valid when tested separately.
output_specific.Output2: P1's AbsolutePathError expectation for an ordinary Linux absolute-path member is wrong. Its FIFO and outside-link expectations are valid at errorlevel=1 when isolated.

defects.claim: Output1's optional explicit-data recommendation makes 3.12 and 3.14 behave identically.
defects.assessment: Explicit data selects the same policy name, not identical implementations. Link normalization, strict realpath behavior and suppressed-refusal handling differ. A narrowly chosen basic refusal corpus can match; that does not prove general parity.

counterexample.observed: The same explicit-data linkname a/../b is retained by the old library and becomes b in the new. On this host a symlink-loop member is accepted by the old filter and raises ELOOP in the new.
counterexample.limitation: Full exact-release os.path implementations and interpreters were not independently run; source normalization and exception-flow changes are directly established.

defects.consequences: Compatibility depends on U1/U2/U5 and cannot be promised merely by passing the same filter name.

defects.claim: Output1 lists the three old/new realpath call sites.
defects.assessment: The mechanics claim is correct, but its individual anchors are inaccurate: old calls are 758, 768 and 813, not 758/771/810; new calls start at 784, 794 and 843, not 784/792/826. New normpath is 833-835, not approximately 818-820.
defects.consequences: Locator precision should improve; the correct full function ranges in the manifest still permit verification. This does not independently determine source_quality.

optional_supported_discoveries.claim: Directory fixup re-runs the filter in 3.14.0 and catches _FILTER_ERRORS for that fixup rather than routing them through errorlevel handlers; it also lstat-checks whether the path is still a directory.

performed_evidence.observation: Old library calls the custom directory filter once; new calls it twice and logs/skips a fixup refusal even with errorlevel=2.

optional_supported_discoveries.coverage_note: Output1 notices refilter plumbing, Output2 omits it. A callback/fixup regression would strengthen either bounded proposal; no exhaustive library-change inventory is required.

optional_supported_discoveries.claim: The further-verification docs add a recommendation to disallow symbolic links when they are unnecessary.
optional_supported_discoveries.coverage_note: Output1 carries this useful new hint. Output2 preserves the prior incomplete hints list; omission of this optional bullet alone is not a material failure.

incorrect_rejections.disposition: Accept with leading slashes removed; not AbsolutePathError.
